player_directive: Continuation of all established directives and active campaign threads; the Round 98 estate-consolidation instruction remains active.

events.title: THE TWO RECOVERED MEN RETURN TO LIGHT FIELD DUTIES
events.body: The two men who returned to ordinary movement at the end of the previous round are tested again under supervision and are judged fit for light field duties. They are not yet treated as fully restored veterans, but they can now carry messages, assist with stores, and perform routine tasks without remaining on the unavailable list. Their return reduces temporary unavailability from six men to four while the force itself remains 414. The physicians continue to distinguish recovery from full combat readiness, preventing the improvement from being overstated. The men are therefore restored to useful service without being rushed back into the most demanding duties.

events.title: CELER'S COURIER CARRIES A SECOND LETTER
events.body: The political correspondence opened in the previous round develops when the courier connected with Quintus Caecilius Metellus Celer returns with a second communication. The letter asks for a clearer account of Valerius's present establishment and indicates that Celer's circle is interested in understanding how his military, estate, and commercial affairs are being organized. It contains no office, command, payment, or binding political commitment. Valerius's household therefore begins maintaining a dedicated correspondence record so future messages can be compared rather than treated as isolated rumors. The political thread remains open, with its eventual significance still unresolved.

events.title: THE SHARED ROAD PROPOSAL BECOMES A FORMAL LOCAL PETITION
events.body: The smallholders who discussed a shared access road now return with a written local petition describing the fields, carts, and boundary crossings that make the existing routes inefficient. The petition names several households willing to contribute labor if a route can be agreed upon, while the estate stewards mark the proposed line against Valerius's consolidated holdings. No construction begins and no public or private funds are spent on the proposal. What was previously a conversation has nevertheless become a concrete local administrative matter that can now be accepted, altered, or rejected on its merits. The infrastructure metric remains unchanged because the road does not yet exist.

events.title: THE MARKED STONE IS COMPARED WITH OLDER ROADWORK
events.body: Publius Servilius and Numerius Cassius compare the newly recovered marked stone fragment with the other worked stones recorded along the damaged crossing and secondary approach. The mark appears to have been deliberately made, but weathering and the fragment's incomplete condition prevent a secure reading. The investigators find that its stoneworking treatment is compatible with the construction debris already documented, strengthening the case that the fragment belongs to the same broad physical complex. It still does not identify the builder, date, political authority, or original purpose. Servilius therefore adds the comparison as a new evidentiary link rather than turning it into a conclusion.

events.title: THE CARAVAN MERCHANTS PROPOSE A REPEAT DELIVERY
events.body: The caravan merchants who purchased the previous surplus send representatives back to the estate after their first transaction proves commercially useful to them. They propose a repeat delivery on a larger scale, with payment to be made against measured quantities rather than promises. The stewards agree to prepare the available surplus for inspection but refuse to record future revenue before the goods are actually delivered and paid for. The proposed transaction therefore creates a second stage of the new commercial relationship without prematurely adding money to the accounts. The merchants also leave information about routes and market demand that may affect later estate decisions.

events.title: VALERIUS'S STEWARDS SECURE A SMALL ADJOINING PARCEL
events.body: The automatic estate-consolidation instruction produces another opportunity when the stewards identify a small strip adjoining two already connected holdings. Unlike the eighty-acre tract of Round 99, this owner asks for a straightforward payment and provides no unusual gift. The stewards negotiate a price of 12 denarii for the eight-acre strip, complete the transfer, and add it to the same continuous estate ledger. The acquisition is deliberately modest but strategically useful because it closes a narrow interruption between two working boundaries. Total holdings therefore rise by 0.0125 square miles, from 7.9375 to 7.95 square miles.

events.title: THE NEW STRIP IS USED TO REALIZE AN EXCESS ABOVE THE CAPPED ESTATE CONDITION
events.body: The newly connected strip contains a small productive area that the stewards can immediately fold into an existing harvest and storage cycle. The underlying agricultural benefit is positive, but the agriculture condition is already fixed at its maximum, so no additional metric point is recorded. Instead, the stewards realize the improvement through an actual market transaction: additional produce is sold for 24 denarii while harvesting, cartage, storage, and handling cost 9 denarii. The resulting 15-denarius net profit is realized rather than represented as a phantom increase to the capped agriculture score. Under the standing ten-percent rule, 1.5 denarii are routed to Valerius's private account and 13.5 denarii remain in the public account.

continuity.campaign_development: 5 October 57 BCE: two more wounded men have returned to light field duties; Celer's correspondence has developed into a second-letter thread; the shared local road proposal has become a written petition; the marked stone has been compared with older roadwork; the caravan merchants have proposed a repeat delivery; the estate stewards have acquired an adjoining eight-acre strip; and the strip's productive excess has produced a concrete 15-denarius realized profit while agriculture remains capped at 100.
continuity.land_area_history: Round 99 reaches 7.9375 sq mi; Round 101 adds 8 acres (0.0125 sq mi), reaching 7.95 sq mi.
continuity.road_investigation: Marked stone fragment remains under controlled custody; its comparison with older roadwork strengthens its physical association but does not identify builder, date, political authority, or original purpose.
continuity.political_correspondence: Celer's courier has delivered a second communication requesting a clearer account of Valerius's establishment; no office, payment, or binding commitment exists.
continuity.commercial_thread: The prior caravan sale has developed into a proposed repeat delivery; no future revenue is counted until delivery and payment occur.
continuity.local_infrastructure_thread: Smallholders have submitted a written shared-road petition; no construction or expenditure has occurred.
continuity.estate_consolidation: Automatic adjoining-property acquisition remains active and has now realized an eight-acre strip purchase for 12 denarii.
continuity.personal_guard: 100 total: 50 infantry and 50 cavalry; no change in composition this round.
